clue.text: You get a minute portion for each boy

parts.note: a second is a small portion of a minute
per means for each, as in miles per hour
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A father hands out tiny equal shares of something to each of his boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You' is the definition: in grammar, 'you' is the pronoun of the second of the three persons.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the pronoun used to address the listener belongs to the second of three persons.

clue.text: Ease tension by creating shortage in Indonesian currency

indicators.note: in tells us the word for shortage sits inside the currency name

parts.note: the sen is a small coin of Indonesia, a hundredth of a rupiah
a lack is a shortage

explanation.surface: A financial report blames a cash shortage for easing economic tension in Indonesia.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen a rope or relax pressure is to make it less tight, which eases tension.

clue.text: In catering much effort is required of him

definitions.text: In catering much effort is required of him

indicators.note: In tells us the answer lies tucked within the words that follow in the clue

explanation.surface: Someone working in catering has to put in a great deal of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'much' into the start of 'effort', and the whole clue also describes the kitchen worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook running a kitchen is the person in catering from whom hard work is demanded.

clue.text: Nicked from honourable man in well-known surroundings

indicators.note: in well-known surroundings means the honourable man is enclosed by the word for well-known

parts.note: noted means well-known
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Something was stolen from a respected gentleman in a famous setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicked' looks like British slang for stolen, but here it means cut with small notches.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with small cuts in its edge has been nicked, marked with V-shaped cuts.

clue.text: Complete one's training and get an exeat

definitions.meaning: cadets finish their course with a parade marking the end of training
an exeat is leave to be absent, and a ... is a permit to leave and come back

explanation.walkthrough: An exeat is the permission a British boarding school gives a pupil to spend time away.
explanation.definitionFit: Military cadets parade at the end of their course, and a pass to leave temporarily lets one go out.

clue.text: Sally is right to help

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally is entitled to lend a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name, but it is a sudden attack or sortie.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden attacking rush out from a defended place, much like a surprise attack.

clue.text: Return ticket to the Australian bush

definitions.meaning: a return ticket takes you out and then back

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is playful: split the answer into two words describing a round trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A return trip goes out and comes back, and the remote Australian interior bears that name.

clue.text: Loving endearments from close relations

definitions.meaning: affectionate words of the kind used between lovers
being on very familiar footing with someone

explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is only a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Being very close friends means being on familiar footing, and affectionate words are the language of such closeness.

clue.text: Nineteen moles tumbling around with huge enjoyment

indicators.note: tumbling around suggests the letters of the two words being thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A lot of moles roll about in the earth, having a wonderful time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumbling around' rearranges the letters of NINETEEN MOLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in their element is thoroughly happy and at ease, enjoying themselves greatly.

clue.text: Dine in the snuggery. It's most orderly

indicators.note: in tells us the word for dine goes inside the cosy place

parts.note: a snuggery is a cosy retreat, a nest
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: An invitation to dinner in a cosy room, praised as the tidiest place.
explanation.definitionFit: The tidiest arrangement is the most orderly, the superlative of trim.

clue.text: Fascinated by a small glove

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a mitten is a kind of glove

explanation.surface: Someone is captivated by a tiny little glove.
explanation.definitionFit: To be smitten is to be infatuated, captivated, struck with love.

clue.text: I meet North Kentucky black

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: A traveller describes going to meet someone in the north of Kentucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dark as writing fluid is very dark in colour, close to black.

clue.text: Disorder is enormous after tea

indicators.note: after places the word for enormous behind the word for tea

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
OS stands for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: A huge mess has arisen following afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete confusion and lack of order is disorder at its worst.

clue.text: One in leading position is too puffed up

indicators.note: in tells us the numeral for one goes inside the front position

parts.note: the van, short for vanguard, is the leading position
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone at the head of things has become rather too self-important.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceited person is puffed up with pride about themselves.

clue.text: One of limited vision states 'is aspiration

indicators.note: states means the phrase is said out loud, in an accent dropping the h

parts.note: a speaker dropping the h, as the apostrophe shows

explanation.surface: A short-sighted man declares what his ambition is, in a broad accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''is' signals h-dropping, so the man saying 'my hope' drops the h too; aspiration is also the name for the h sound itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-sighted person sees only nearby things clearly, so their vision is limited.

clue.text: Keep English on as a special skill

parts.note: a keep is the stronghold of a castle, a fort

explanation.surface: A teacher urges keeping English going as a particular talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb but is the noun, a castle's strong tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's strong point is the thing they are especially good at.

clue.text: Refusal by you to enter also caused irritation

indicators.note: to enter means the refusal and the old word for you go inside the word for also

parts.note: and means also, in addition
no is a refusal
ye is an old word for you

explanation.surface: Being turned down by you when trying to get in too was irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: If something irked someone, it vexed them, causing irritation.

clue.text: Order a risk to be taken with Russian vehicles

indicators.note: order means the letters are put into a fresh sequence

explanation.surface: Someone takes a risk by ordering transport in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' rearranges the letters of A RISK TO.
explanation.definitionFit: These are Russian carriages drawn by three horses abreast.

clue.text: Model once of generous proportions

parts.note: ex means former, once
ample means large and generous in size

explanation.surface: A former model who was rather large in build.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests a fashion model, but it means a pattern or specimen to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A model to copy is a pattern or instance that illustrates the type.

clue.text: Averse to getting in a pious man

indicators.note: in tells us the word for getting goes inside the article and the saint

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a pious man
gain means acquisition, getting

explanation.surface: A holy man is reluctant to be involved in acquiring wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed to something means being averse to it.

clue.text: Points for Anglicans to implement

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: Points of doctrine for Anglicans are to be put into practice.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a law or rule into effect is to implement it.

clue.text: Tom's cry of derision

parts.note: a tom is a male feline, so his cry could be read as a feline's call, which is also a jeering whistle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name, but a tom is a male cat, so his cry is a cat's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill whistle or shout of disapproval from a crowd is a jeering cry of derision.

clue.text: Occasion to go over large part of church

indicators.note: in a down clue going over means the first word sits above the next

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity, an occasion

explanation.surface: An opportunity to look over a big section of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The area near the altar reserved for clergy and choir is the eastern part of a church.

clue.text: Old net I can repair

indicators.note: repair suggests mending, and the letters are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A fisherman offers to mend an old net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair' rearranges the letters of NET I CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very old dates from long ago, of great age.

clue.text: Dash to bring back new beer

indicators.note: to bring back means the word for beer is turned the other way round

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Someone rushes off to return a new bottle of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring back' turns ALE into ELA; the N follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash in the sense of verve and flair is style and spirit.

clue.text: No longer keen on Albert getting cheap meat

parts.note: to go off something is to stop liking it
Al is the short form of Albert

explanation.surface: Albert has lost interest in eating budget cuts of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Organ meats such as liver and kidneys are inexpensive cuts of animal flesh.

clue.text: A hundred in total? Rubbish!

indicators.note: in tells us the numeral for a hundred goes inside the word for total

parts.note: a sum is a total
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a claimed total of a hundred as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating filth on a liquid, or worthless people, is refuse, rubbish.

clue.text: The case for some private tuition?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question about whether private lessons are justified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The case for' reads as an argument in favour, but 'The case' is the definition, a small needle holder.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small ornamental holder for needles and other sewing items.

clue.text: Soldering tin and silver presents a problem

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Joining tin and silver with solder turns out to be tricky.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an unexpected difficulty or obstacle.

clue.text: Drive around Islington to get VDU

indicators.note: around means the word for drive surrounds the postcode letters

parts.note: to motor is to drive
Islington is in London's N1 postal district, read as the letters NI

explanation.surface: Driving round a London borough to collect a computer screen.
explanation.walkthrough: N1 is the London postcode for Islington; the figure 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A visual display unit is a computer screen, also called a display screen.

clue.text: Is incapable even of finding a place to eat

parts.note: can't means is unable, is incapable
e'en is a poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: Someone is unable even to find somewhere to have a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a dining hall in a workplace or school.

clue.text: Test match produces cry of astonishment

definitions.meaning: trying out a match by striking it to make a flame
an old-fashioned British exclamation of surprise

explanation.walkthrough: 'Test match' looks like an international cricket match, but here it means testing a matchstick.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking a match to see if it works produces a flame, and the phrase is also a dated exclamation of surprise.
